To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we isolated and identified a novel AHL-degrading bacterial strain from the potato rhizosphere, which has potential to suppress the virulence of the potato pathogen, Pectobacteriurn atrosepticum, by degrading its AHL signal molecule.

we have identified a novel N-AHL degradative enzyme, AHL lactonase, from a soil bacterium, Arthrobacter sp. strain EM83 and demonstrated the ability of this enzyme to inhibit the pathogenicity and virulence factor expression of Pectobacterum atrosepticum.
we isolated and characterized N-AHL degraders from the potato rhizosphere and that these isolates can be used to control bacterial soft rot in potato.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diversity of bacteria which can degrade AHLs, the identification of AHL-degrading bacteria and the application of these bacteria to control plant pathogens.
the isolation and identification of N-AHL degraders from potato rhizosphere, and the biological control of potato tuber soft rot caused by Pectobacteria.
the isolation of N-AHL-degrading bacteria from the rhizosphere soil and the screening of their biocontrol ability against Pectobacteriaceae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of QS interfering bacteria is a promising approach to control bacterial soft rot disease.
the use of QS interfering bacteria is a promising approach for biological control of plant diseases.
the use of N-AHL degraders to control plant pathogens is a promising strategy to control diseases caused by plant pathogens that utilize AHL-based QS systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-AHL degraders can be used as biocontrol agents against plant pathogen P. atrosepticum.
the N-AHL degrader Bacillus sp. strain EM84 can be used as a biocontrol agent to control soft rot disease caused by Pectobactera carotovorum subsp. atrosepticum in potato.
the N-AHL degradative bacteria in the rhizophere could be used for the biological control of bacterial diseases in potato.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified several bacteria that degrade N-AHLs in the potato rhizosphere, which may be useful for the development of new biocontrol agents against Pectobacteriaceae.
the use of QS signal inhibitors to control plant diseases may provide a novel approach to plant protection.
there are many bacteria in nature that can interfere with QS and these bacteria could be used to control pathogens.
